ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the equilateral $\triangle ABC$, D is the midpoint of $AB$, $DE \perp AC$ at point E, and $EF \perp BC$ at point F. Given $AB=8$, what is the length of $BF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle and $D$ is the midpoint of $AB$,\\
thus $\angle A=\angle C=60^\circ$, and $AC=AB=BC=8$, with $AD=\frac{1}{2}AB=4$,\\
since $DE\perp AC$ and $EF\perp BC$,\\
thus $\angle AED=\angle CFE=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle EDA=\angle FEC=30^\circ$,\\
hence $AE=\frac{1}{2}AD=2$,\\
therefore $CE=AC-AE=8-2=6$, and $CF=\frac{1}{2}CE=3$,\\
thus $BF=BC-CF=8-3=\boxed{5}$;

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:

since $DE\perp AC$ and $EF\perp BC$,\\

therefore $\angle EDA=\angle FEC=30^\circ$,\\
hence $AE=\frac{1}{2}AD=2$,\\
therefore $CE=AC-AE=8-2=6$, and $CF=\frac{1}{2}CE=3$,\\
thus $BF=BC-CF=8-3=\boxed{5}$;
